newsitem.title: REPUBLIC OF IRELAND: HORSE RACING-SECOND ARC HOPEFUL OUT OF BIG RACE.
newsitem.headline: HORSE RACING-SECOND ARC HOPEFUL OUT OF BIG RACE.

text.p: Another notable contender for the Prix de l'Arc de Triomphe fell by the wayside on Wednesday when the connections of Timarida unexpectedly scrapped plans to enter the filly for the big Longchamp race on October 6.
Timarida, owned by the Aga Khan, will instead head for the Champion Stakes at Newmarket on October 19.
Quoted at 12-1, the filly's absence follows Tuesday's news that English-trained Riyadian, also 12-1, would not run because of injury.
A spokesman for Timarida's trainer John Oxx said it was felt the two-furlong (400 metres) shorter distance of the Champion Stakes would suit Timarida better.

Timarida, successful in five countries, took her win and place earnings past 600,000 pounds ($938,600) barrier when putting the Epsom Derby winner Shaamit firmly in his place in the Irish Champion Stakes at Leopardstown earlier this month.
French-trained Helissio is the 3-1 favourite for the Longchamp race, Europe's richest, followed by Irish Derby winner Zagreb at 5-1.
